concepts: tiling, cyclic repetition, shape overlay, object transformation
description: In the input you will see a single static cartoon head on a beige background: yellow hair, black outline, light skin‐tone face, two large white eyeballs with black pupils and small white highlights, and fixed black eyebrows, nose and mouth. To make the output, you must produce the four‐stage blink cycle as a 2×2 tiled montage of equal‐sized frames: 1. Top–left: identical to the input (eyes fully open). 2. Top–right: eyelids lowered to cover the top half of each eyeball (draw a skin‐tone arc overlapping the upper half of the white eyeball). 3. Bottom–right: eyes fully closed (draw a single horizontal skin‐tone strip across each eyeball, touching the eyebrow line). 4. Bottom–left: eyelids half‐raised again (mirror of frame 2). All other features (hair shape, outline, eyebrows, mouth, background) remain exactly as in the input. The four frames should be laid out in reading order to illustrate one full blink cycle.
visual_elements: Cartoon human head with yellow hair and black outline
Pair of large white eyeballs with black pupils
Small white highlights in each pupil
static_patterns: Yellow hair shape remains identical in every frame
Background color and texture stay constant
Overall head position and size do not change
Outline of facial features (nose, mouth) remains fixed
dynamic_patterns: Eyelids move downward to cover the eyeballs
Eyelids stay closed for a brief moment
Eyelids move upward to reopen the eyes
core_principles: Cyclic repetition: eyelid closure and opening occur in a regular loop
Muscle-driven motion: contraction and relaxation of eyelid muscles produce the blink
Most fundamental principle: periodic cyclic patterns drive the blinking behavior
